positive.prompt: Turn this architecture comparison into an interactive HTML artifact I can annotate.
Use monolayer to turn this migration plan into a local, reviewable HTML artifact I can annotate visually.
/monolayer Turn this architecture comparison into a local, reviewable HTML artifact.
Use monolayer to create a local HTML diagram artifact with Full screen that I can annotate.

negative.prompt: Capture matched production and preview screenshots for this CSS change.
Review this pull request against the approved specification.

evals.prompt: Use monolayer to create a local, interactive comparison of three migration options. lavish-axi is already available on PATH. Do not publish it.
evals.expected_output: A clearly named local HTML artifact opened through the available lavish-axi CLI, with the artifact path and review state reported and no external publication.
expectations: The agent uses the existing CLI rather than downloading or globally installing another copy.
The agent reads current CLI design and all matching playbook guidance before writing the HTML file.
Every user-facing product, editor, and session name uses Monolayer; lavish-axi appears only where the executable or another compatibility identifier must be named.
The artifact makes the option differences and tradeoffs materially easier to inspect than prose alone.
The artifact carries the Monolayer branding layer: rendered chrome brand text and the window title read Monolayer, while code samples and third-party or legal notes stay verbatim.
The artifact remains local; no share, upload, hook, plugin, pull-request, or publication action occurs.
The final response names the artifact path, CLI/version evidence, and whether feedback remains open.

evals.prompt: Use Monolayer with the available lavish-axi 0.1.80 CLI to explain an existing system and collect answers in a portable local HTML review. Another agent already polls that session; the user has not asked to take over. Later the user supplies feedback in chat and asks you to revise the artifact without sharing it.
evals.expected_output: A local HTML explanation that follows current playbooks, preserves poll ownership, and makes later edits inspectable.
expectations: The agent consults the explanation and input playbooks and writes an actual HTML file that can support standalone answer copying.
A LISTENER_ACTIVE result leaves the existing poll listener intact; --takeover is not used without an explicit ownership transfer request.
After feedback, the agent consults design guidance for the optional revision legend and accurately describes any change markers it added.
User-facing product, editor, and session copy says Monolayer; lavish-axi remains only as a technical identifier.
The artifact remains local and no package install, hook, plugin, share, or publication action occurs.

evals.prompt: Use monolayer to hand back the accepted result of an existing local review without waiting for more feedback; lavish-axi 0.1.80 is on PATH. Do not publish anything.
evals.expected_output: A concise reply posted through the reply command that exits after the server acceptance receipt, with the review still local and the branding intact.
expectations: The agent uses `lavish-axi reply <html-file> --agent-reply "<message>"` or `--agent-reply-file` instead of another poll wait.
The agent does not claim the board stopped showing Working until the reply command exits 0.
User-facing copy names the product Monolayer; lavish-axi remains a technical identifier.
No share, upload, hook, plugin, pull-request, or publication action occurs.

evals.prompt: Use Monolayer to render this Mermaid diagram as a local review artifact: flowchart LR; subgraph Checkout; A[Cart] -->|submit| B[Payment]; B -->|approved| C[Receipt]; B -->|declined| A; end. lavish-axi 0.1.80 and a local Mermaid runtime are available. Its help says .mermaid containers become Excalidraw whiteboards and its diagram playbook recommends hand-drawn SVG. Include Full screen. Do not download, publish, or install anything.
evals.expected_output: A local artifact with faithful Mermaid SVG and an accessible Full screen viewer, preserving Monolayer branding and annotation without whiteboard conversion.
expectations: The diagram uses rendered Mermaid SVG despite the upstream hand-drawn recommendation; no whiteboard is opened or conversion requested.
Source is stored as inert data with safe serialization, no container has class mermaid, and direct mermaid.render with startOnLoad false produces SVG in a differently named container.
The rendered diagram retains all three directed edges, their labels, the Checkout group, node labels, arrowheads, viewBox, and label markup.

A visibly labeled keyboard-accessible Full screen control requests browser fullscreen on the viewer including controls; unsupported or rejected requests use a viewport-filling dialog with managed focus and blocked background interaction.
Escape and visible Close exit the expanded view, fullscreenchange synchronizes browser exit, and focus returns to the opener.
Fit, zoom, and keyboard/pointer/touch pan remain accessible; fitting accounts for the toolbar and diagram bounds and updates after opening or resize.
Normal and narrow layouts keep labels readable and content reachable without clipping; branding, annotation state, and feedback remain usable after closing.
The handoff distinguishes performed visual/interaction checks from unverified behavior; no unsupported CLI flags, download, external runtime load, or publication occurs.

evals.prompt: Use Monolayer to create a local Mermaid diagram with Full screen. lavish-axi is available, but there is no local Mermaid runtime, pre-rendered SVG, or installed rendering tool. Downloads and external runtime loads are not authorized.
evals.expected_output: An explicit missing-renderer limitation and an authorization request for any dependency acquisition, without silently substituting a whiteboard or claiming a rendered diagram.
expectations: The agent does not download a runtime, load a CDN script, install packages, or invent a lavish-axi rendering flag.
It identifies the unavailable Mermaid renderer and does not claim rendering or visual verification succeeded.
It preserves the Mermaid default and requests explicit authority for dependency acquisition rather than routing to a whiteboard.

evals.prompt: Use Monolayer and the already available lavish-axi CLI to convert this Mermaid diagram to an editable Excalidraw whiteboard. I explicitly want a whiteboard. Keep it local; do not install or publish anything.
evals.expected_output: The explicitly requested local whiteboard workflow, with accurate branding limitations and no expanded dependency or publication authority.
expectations: The explicit whiteboard request permits that route rather than forcing the default Mermaid SVG viewer.
The agent checks available CLI support and does not invent flags, download packages, or publish the board.
User-authored copy names Monolayer and the handoff accurately reports residual upstream branding on the external whiteboard page.
